quote.after:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous endpoint argument in this clause. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.

after.claim: (The sublevel and superlevel descriptions.) Let $q\in J^-(S_b)$: there is $s\in S_b$ with $q\le s$; if $q\ne s$ then $t(q)<t(s)=b$ by strict monotonicity [L1], and if $q=s$ then $t(q)=b$. Conversely, if $t(q)\le b$: choose a maximal geodesic through $q$ with future timelike tangent (it is an inextendible future timelike curve, [L5]) and let $s$ be a point of it; by [L1] the values of $t$ along it run from $-\infty$ to $+\infty$, so there is a point $s$ on it with $t(s)=b$; since the geodesic is future-directed, $q\le s$. Hence $J^-(S_b)\subseteq\{t\le b\}\subseteq J^-(S_b)$, and the dual argument gives $J^+(S_a)=\{t\ge a\}$. In particular $J^-(S_b)$ is closed as a level sublevel set of the continuous function $t$.

(Each truncated one-point cone is compact.) Fix $x\in M$ with $t(x)<b$ and set $A:=J^+(x)\cap J^-(S_b)=J^+(x)\cap\{t\le b\}$; it is closed, being the intersection of the closed sets $J^+(x)$ and $\{t\le b\}$ [L2, step 1.1]. It is compact: otherwise, by [L4] applied to the metric space $(M,d_h)$, there are $r_k\in A$ with no convergent subsequence. For each $k$ choose a future causal curve $\gamma_k:[0,1]\to M$ from $x$ to $r_k$ and reparametrize it by $h$-arclength: $\alpha_k:[0,L_k]\to M$, $\alpha_k(0)=x$, $\alpha_k(L_k)=r_k$. The images satisfy $\alpha_k([0,L_k])\subseteq J^+(x)\cap\{t\le b\}$: indeed every point of $\gamma_k$ lies causally between $x$ and $r_k$, so its $t$-value lies between $t(x)$ and $t(r_k)\le b$ by monotonicity [L1]. If the lengths $L_k$ were bounded, then $d_h(x,r_k)\le L_k$ would be bounded, so the $r_k$ would have a convergent subsequence by [L4]: contradiction. Hence $L_k\to\infty$ along a subsequence, and the half-line limit curve lemma [L3] gives a future-inextendible future causal curve $\alpha^+:[0,\infty)\to M$ with $\alpha^+(0)=x$ that is a uniform limit on compact parameter intervals of the curves $\alpha_k$. Every point of $\alpha^+$ is a limit of points with $t$-values at most $b$, so $t(\alpha^+(\tau))\le b$ for all $\tau$ by continuity of $t$. But along the inextendible extension of $\alpha^+$ (which exists by [L5]) the volume time tends to $+\infty$ at the future end [L1], hence $t(\alpha^+(\tau))\to+\infty$ as $\tau\to\infty$: contradiction. Therefore $A$ is compact.

(Finitely many cones over $K$.) For each $x\in K$ choose a point $x^-\ll x$ (possible by [L5]); the sets $I^+(x^-)$ form an open cover of $K$, so finitely many $x_1,\dots,x_m\in K$ have $K\subseteq\bigcup_iI^+(x_i)$. If $y\in J^+(K)$, choose $x\in K$ with $x\le y$ and $i$ with $x\in I^+(x_i)$; then $x_i\le x\le y$ by transitivity, so $y\in J^+(x_i)$. Hence $J^+(K)\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^mJ^+(x_i)$ and $$J^+(K)\cap J^-(S_b)\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^m\bigl(J^+(x_i)\cap\{t\le b\}\bigr).$$ Each of the finitely many sets on the right is compact by step 2.1 (it is empty if $t(x_i)>b$, a singleton if $t(x_i)=b$, and the set $A$ of step 2.1 if $t(x_i)<b$), so the union is compact; the set $J^+(K)\cap J^-(S_b)$ is closed by [L2] and step 1.1, and a closed subset of a compact set is compact. This proves the statement together with step 1.1.
